exposure: Natural rearing by sow (for term reference pigs)
outcome: Brain development (ex vivo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) endpoints)
Gene expression (related to sialic acid metabolism, myelination, ganglioside biosynthesis in hippocampus)
cohort: Pigs (of either sex) delivered by cesarean section at 90% gestation, and term piglets used as reference groups.
finding: Sialyllactose supplementation significantly improved spatial cognition in preterm pigs, approaching the cognition level of term reference pigs, and upregulated hippocampal genes related to sialic acid metabolism, myelination, and ganglioside biosynthesis.
mod_finding: Sialic acid levels in the hippocampus and MRI endpoints were strongly influenced by postconceptional age and postnatal rearing conditions, which included a comparison between artificially reared term piglets and vaginally born, naturally reared piglets.
